extracted.intended_audience: Members of Congress, congressional staff, and policymakers overseeing federal competitive sourcing/A-76 policy
extracted.subtask_description: Policy options and evaluative criteria for Congress to consider when assessing and reforming OMB Circular A-76 competitive sourcing competitions (with emphasis on the Walter Reed A-76 experience and military medical facilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require specific reporting on the status of ongoing A-76 competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress may direct DOD to provide more detailed information on the status of ongoing A-76 studies, including quarterly updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested reporting items (verbatim bullets from the page): • the number of older competitions under review, and whether these competitions have been granted waivers; • the status of new standard multi-function A-76 studies, including how many competitions are in excess of the 12-months limitation, and how many have been granted waivers; • the number of competitions that are in excess of 18 months, with or without waivers; • the number of competitions in excess of 30-months, with or without waivers; and • the demographics of the affected government employees in A-76 competitions, and whether any particular group of employees are adversely impacted by the A-76 policy, competition process or the final outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit establishment of numerical quotas for A-76 studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress could prohibit the establishment of numerical quotas for federal agencies conducting A-76 studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale given: some argue that desire to meet numerical quotas (or targets) may have driven decisions to continue problematic competitions (e.g., the Army’s choice to continue Walter Reed competition despite evolving problems). Reference: proposed Section 323 of H.R. 4986.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare activities at military medical facilities to be inherently governmental (or bar competitions there)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress could declare that any activities on military medical facilities that affect patient care would be considered inherently governmental and not appropriate for competition, or prohibit competitions at military medical facilities (including a possible one-year moratorium).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and legislative options included: • Declare all activities at military medical facilities as 'inherently governmental' and not subject to competition; • A one-year moratorium on future A-76 competitions at military medical facilities (example: amendment proposed by Rep. Solomon Ortiz in H.R. 1538, Wounded Warrior Assistance Act of 2007). Policy rationale: activities that touch the military patient may be critical to mission and morale and thus inappropriate for outsourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude health care and retirement costs from A-76 cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress could prohibit the inclusion of health care and retirement costs in the A-76 cost comparison process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context/guidance: Reportedly the Army failed to exclude health care costs as required by the Defense Appropriations bill where DOD contributed more per employee for health care insurance than the contractor; exclusion of retirement costs might preclude rewarding contractors who provide lesser benefits than the federal government. Reference: proposed Section 322 of H.R. 4986.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a rotating team of experienced acquisition professionals to serve as Agency Tender Officials (ATOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a pool/team of experienced A-76 professionals who could be called upon to serve as ATOs in competitions outside their assigned agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested features: ATOs selected to serve in competitions across agencies, require sufficient funds to represent federal employees throughout the competition (including post-award), and may require a certain independence. Rationale: in complex competitions no single individual had overall authority; shared/fragmented authorities led to confusion and lack of effective advocacy for employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require enforcement of A-76 rules and oversight when rules are not followed
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress could ensure that the rules governing A-76 studies are followed and that there is authority to enforce compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: OMB could have stopped the Walter Reed competition when it exceeded permitted length; DOD could have stopped it per law; Army could have excluded health care costs as required by Appropriations Act. Enforcement of rules is presented as necessary to maintain integrity and public confidence; failure to enforce may change outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant federal employees direct protest rights and parity with contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress could grant federal employees the same protest rights as private sector contractors (or improve the ATO protest mechanism) and ensure employees have effective representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background: historically contractors had GAO protest rights while federal employees could not; P.L. 108-375 expanded 'interested party' to include ATOs who may file protests, but ATOs lacked standing in some pre-2003 cases. Options suggested: grant federal employees direct protest rights; ensure agencies cannot conduct competitions unless they have enough money to fund competitions entirely, including representation for federal employees during all phases up to post-award. Rationale: lack of direct protest rights disadvantaged federal employees and contributed to inequity in outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage alternatives to A-76 such as developing High-Performing Organizations (HPOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress could provide incentives to agencies to explore alternatives (e.g., HPOs) to achieve efficiencies sought through A-76 without the costs and challenges of competitive outsourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting citation: GAO’s Commercial Activities Panel (CAP) recommendation to create HPOs. Rationale: with federal employees winning the majority of competitions, agencies might pursue alternatives that do not entail A-76 costs/challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancel outstanding A-76 studies conducted under the pre-2003 Circular
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress could direct the cancellation of any outstanding competitions conducted under the pre-2003 A-76 Circular to avoid problems similar to Walter Reed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: AFGE recommended cancellation of the A-76 study at Keesler AFB; media report cited competitions taking many years (e.g., at least eight years). Rationale: long, flawed pre-2003 competitions risk repeating Walter Reed–style problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit use of A-76 where mission-critical constraints exist and ensure funding and continuity during transitions/BRAC
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 should not be applied universally; competitions may be inappropriate when there are constrained resources, BRAC actions, or combat operations that threaten mission performance. Additionally, when BRAC/realignment is occurring, leadership/time should not be diverted and funding should be provided to maintain full operations until closure or integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text guidance and recommendations: • The A-76 process may be ill-suited for activities affecting military health care; some argue base operations support in medical settings should be exempt. • Given BRAC and combat operations, agencies may lack resources to conduct competitions properly; decisions to continue competitions under such conditions may be unwise. • Recommendation to Secretary of Defense: seek legislative approval to accelerate BRAC implementation (accelerate/waive EIS) and release monies to start construction of the new WRNMMC so existing facilities are not allowed to 'die on the vine'; funding must be provided to maintain full operation until the day of closure.
